_meta.purpose: Category-specific legal clocks, document checklists and escalation ladders. Every clock carries `verify` because a limitation period quoted wrongly is worse than none. The UI labels all of this as guidance, never as advice.
_meta.sources: Statutory periods are cross-referenced to the sections in data/laws/. Portal URLs are official government portals and must be re-checked before production (npm run verify:laws reports on them).

deadlines.label: PIO reply due
deadlines.from: date the application was received (or transferred in)

deadlines.label: Life / personal liberty reply due
deadlines.from: date of receipt
deadlines.conditional: only when the information concerns life or personal liberty

deadlines.label: First appeal
deadlines.from: day 31 (no reply) or the date the reply was received
deadlines.condonation: delay can be condoned for sufficient cause

deadlines.label: First appellate order due
deadlines.from: receipt of the first appeal
deadlines.extension: extendable once, for reasons in writing

deadlines.label: Second appeal to the Information Commission
deadlines.from: the date the appellate decision was (or should have been) received

checklist: Written application (English / Hindi / local language) with one subject per application
Particulars of the applicant - name and address (phone optional)
Prescribed fee proof: Indian currency note, cash receipt, postal receipt, demand draft or online payment receipt from rtionline.gov.in
BPL certificate copy if claiming fee exemption
Numbered list of the information sought - dates, file names, amounts, periods
Copy of the earlier application, its date of posting and the tracking number
Preferred form of the reply (certified copies / inspection / soft copy) and the delivery method

escalation.where: Public Information Officer of the office that holds the record
escalation.note: Central bodies can be filed online; state bodies usually need the state portal or paper.

escalation.where: First Appellate Authority (officer senior to the PIO)
escalation.note: No fee. Within 30 days.

escalation.where: Central Information Commission
escalation.note: Second appeal within 90 days, free; penalty and disciplinary action can be sought.

escalation.where: State Information Commission (for state subjects)
escalation.note: Name of the state commission varies; search '<State> State Information Commission'.

escalation.where: High Court writ (Article 226) where the Commission itself is non-functional or the order is being ignored
escalation.note: Get a lawyer before this step.

deadlines.label: File the consumer complaint
deadlines.from: the date the cause of action arose (delivery, refusal, bill date)
deadlines.condonation: admission after 2 years requires sufficient cause

deadlines.label: Appeal a District Commission order
deadlines.from: the date of the order / copy received

deadlines.label: E-commerce grievance officer must acknowledge
deadlines.from: your written complaint

checklist: Invoice / order confirmation / payment proof (card statement screenshot is acceptable)
Delivered product with the defect photographed (and the packaging, labels and warranty card)
Every communication with the seller: email threads, chat transcripts, call recordings, ticket numbers
Written rejection or non-response from the seller or brand
Repair job sheets, inspection reports, or a doctor's / technician's opinion on the defect
For services: agreement / purchase order, service report, bill, and the specific deficiency described
Identity proof of the complainant, and the seller's registered address from their website footer
A computation of the amount claimed (refund + interest + compensation + cost)

escalation.where: Written demand to the seller/service provider (keep the letter generated here)
escalation.note: Give 15 days; keep the postal receipt.

escalation.where: Grievance officer / nodal officer of the platform or brand
escalation.note: Mandatory for marketplaces under the E-Commerce Rules.

escalation.where: National Consumer Helpline
escalation.note: Free; also 1915 / 1800-11-1550. Good for mediation and for a record of the complaint.

escalation.where: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (online filing)
escalation.note: Fee is modest and refundable if the complaint succeeds.

escalation.where: State Commission (appeal above the District limit) and NCDRC
escalation.note: Pecuniary limits are revised by notification - confirm before filing.

deadlines.label: Employer must pay wages for the month
deadlines.from: the last day of the wage period (10 days in larger establishments)

deadlines.label: Claim for unlawful deduction / delayed wages
deadlines.from: the date the deduction came to your knowledge or wages fell due
deadlines.condonation: extendable for sufficient cause - confirm the current limit

deadlines.label: POSH complaint to the Internal Committee
deadlines.from: the date of the last incident

deadlines.label: Inquiry must be completed
deadlines.from: the date the complaint is filed

deadlines.label: Retrenchment notice (or wages in lieu)
deadlines.from: the intended date of retrenchment

checklist: Appointment letter / employment contract and any policy you signed
Salary slips for at least the last six months (and the last three showing the shortfall)
Bank statement showing the salary credit and the actual amount received
Attendance records, leave approvals, and the email/letter of termination or suspension
PF/ESI passbook screenshot from the EPFO member portal (for PF complaints)
Written notice of the alleged loss or damage and the show-cause, if any
Name and designation of the manager who took the decision, and the dates
For POSH: the complaint to the IC, its acknowledgment, and the composition of the committee

escalation.where: Written representation to HR and the employer's grievance channel
escalation.note: Keep it factual, attach the payslip math.

escalation.where: Labour Commissioner / the authority appointed under the Payment of Wages Act in your state
escalation.note: Single-window portal for several labour-compliance services.

escalation.where: EPFO Regional P.F. Commissioner (for PF deducted and not deposited)
escalation.note: Grievances can also be filed on the EPFO portal / UMANG.

escalation.where: Labour Court / Industrial Tribunal (dispute referred by the State Government)
escalation.note: A lawyer or union is normally needed from here.

escalation.where: DLSA free legal aid (most employees in this category are eligible)

deadlines.label: Arrested person must be produced before a Magistrate
deadlines.from: the arrest, excluding travel time

deadlines.label: SP/DCP decision after a Sec 175(3)-style written complaint
deadlines.from: the date your written complaint was received
deadlines.law: BNSS (formerly CrPC 154(3)) - practice, not a fixed statutory period
deadlines.note: No statutory clock; 14 days is the customary follow-up interval, not law.

deadlines.label: Writ to the High Court (compelling registration)
deadlines.from: the refusal, as a rule of prudence
deadlines.note: Delay must be explained; earlier is always better.

checklist: A written copy of the information you gave, with the date and time of each visit to the station
Name / rank of the officer you spoke to, and the station's daily-diary (Roznamcha) number if given
Any acknowledgment or receipt you were handed
Evidence: photographs of damage or injury, medical records, CCTV location and time, message and call logs
Names and addresses of witnesses, with their contact numbers
The postal receipt when you write to the SP/DCP (this is the step that most often works)
For an arrest: the memo of arrest, the arrestee's medical condition, and who was informed

escalation.where: Officer in charge of the police station, in person and in writing
escalation.note: Ask for the DD/NCR number even if no FIR is registered.

escalation.where: Superintendent of Police / DCP of the district, by registered post
escalation.note: The statutory route when the station refuses.

escalation.where: State police complaint portal / DGP grievance cell and the CM helpline
escalation.note: Every major state runs an online complaint portal; search '<state> police complaint portal' rather than guessing a URL.

escalation.where: Magistrate having jurisdiction (directing registration / complaint route)
escalation.note: Lawyer strongly recommended; do not guess the BNSS section number.

escalation.where: High Court under Article 226
escalation.note: Writ of mandamus to compel registration.

deadlines.label: Report the unauthorised transaction to keep zero liability
deadlines.from: the date of the transaction (working days)
deadlines.law: RBI Master Direction on compensation for unauthorised electronic banking transactions

deadlines.label: Bank must respond to a written complaint
deadlines.from: the date of the written complaint

deadlines.label: Escalate to the Banking Ombudsman
deadlines.from: receipt of the bank's final reply (or expiry of the 30 days)

deadlines.label: Civil / summary suit for the amount
deadlines.from: when the money became due and refused
deadlines.law: Limitation Act, 1969 (three years for most suits)

checklist: Account statement highlighting the disputed entries with date, amount and reference/UTR number
The SMS, email or app notification for each transaction
Card / UPI details (mask the number in anything you share publicly)
Ticket or reference number of the first complaint to the bank, and every follow-up
Any OTP, device or IP the fraudster may have used, and the time of the fraud
Proof you are the account holder (PAN and address proof, masked where shared online)
Police / cybercrime complaint acknowledgment (needed by the bank to process a fraud claim)

escalation.where: Written complaint to the bank / card issuer (and freeze the card immediately)
escalation.note: The clock for zero liability starts when you notify them.

escalation.where: Nodal / principal officer of the bank, quoting the first complaint number
escalation.note: Lists of nodal officers are published on each bank's website.

escalation.where: RBI Integrated Ombudsman (free, binding up to the notified amount)
escalation.note: Escalate after 30 days of silence or an unsatisfactory reply.

escalation.where: Consumer Commission for deficiency in service
escalation.note: Where the grievance is service deficiency, not just a disputed transaction.

escalation.where: Cyber crime police + bank's nodal officer, in parallel, for fraud by a third party
escalation.note: Reporting fast is the only lever that can trace the money.

deadlines.label: Report to 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in
deadlines.from: the moment you realise the fraud
deadlines.note: The trace is time-critical - money moves out of the mule accounts within minutes.

deadlines.label: Written complaint to the bank
deadlines.from: the transaction date

deadlines.label: Card chargeback / dispute window
deadlines.from: the transaction date (network rules)
deadlines.law: card network + RBI rules - confirm with your bank

checklist: Screenshot of every message, call log, SMS and the app or website used
The phone numbers, UPI IDs, VPA, bank account numbers and QR codes the fraudster used
Transaction reference numbers, dates, amounts and the beneficiary name shown
The URL / Play Store link / invoice and the seller's claimed identity
Do not wipe the phone; note the device model and the OS version
A written timeline of events in your own words, with times
The acknowledgment / complaint ID from cybercrime.gov.in

escalation.where: Dial 1930 or file at the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal
escalation.note: Financial-fraud reports go here; it routes to the State cyber cell.

escalation.where: Written complaint to the bank's nodal officer for the fraudulent credit
escalation.note: Ask for a lien mark on the beneficiary account - the police order enables it.

escalation.where: Local cyber cell / police station FIR (IT Act + BNS provisions)
escalation.note: If refused, use the SP route as in Police / FIR.

escalation.where: Platform / app store takedown and the intermediary's grievance officer
escalation.note: IT Rules require a grievance officer; a written takedown request helps stop reuse.

escalation.where: Consumer Commission (platform's deficiency) or a civil recovery suit
escalation.note: Where the platform's own conduct enabled the loss.

deadlines.label: Notice to determine a lease other than year-to-year
deadlines.from: the date the notice is served (or the contract's period)

deadlines.label: Notice for a yearly / multi-year lease
deadlines.from: the date of service

deadlines.label: Suit for the security deposit
deadlines.from: the date the deposit became refundable and was refused

deadlines.label: Police complaint / injunction when locked out
deadlines.from: the forcible act - move immediately
deadlines.note: Self-help eviction is unlawful; an interim injunction is often granted quickly.

checklist: The rent agreement (signed and, if applicable, registered) and any addendum
Every rent receipt, and bank transfers / UPI history proving payment
Photographs and videos of the property's condition at move-in and at the dispute
The landlord's notice (or the WhatsApp / SMS demanding vacation), with dates
Utility bills in your name, showing you were the occupant
Inventory of belongings and the estimate of any loss or damage
Society / association correspondence where the property is in a building
Written demand for the deposit, with the postal or delivery receipt

escalation.where: Written notice to the landlord / agent (advocate's letterhead where affordable)
escalation.note: Set out the notice period, the deposit math and the deadline.

escalation.where: Police complaint where there is force, intimidation, lock changing or cutting of supply
escalation.note: Use the Police / FIR ladder - including the SP route.

escalation.where: Rent Controller / Court as provided by the applicable state rent law
escalation.note: Name the state law; eviction requires a court order.

escalation.where: Civil court / summary suit for the deposit, or consumer forum where the service was by a builder or agency
escalation.note: Money claims of the size typical of a deposit are usually summary-suit territory.

escalation.where: DLSA free legal aid

deadlines.label: Application for protection / residence / monetary relief
deadlines.from: as soon as the act occurs - there is no waiting period
deadlines.law: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
deadlines.note: No limitation is prescribed; delay only weakens the case.

deadlines.label: Maintenance application (BNS/BNSS provision)
deadlines.from: when the person refuses to maintain
deadlines.note: The BNSS section number must be confirmed before use.

checklist: Marriage certificate or proof of the relationship, and addresses
Income proof of both parties (salary slips, ITR, bank statements)
Every threatening message, call recording and medical record of injury
Proof of the shared household (electricity bill, rent agreement, ration card)
List of stridhan and dowry articles with the bills, and where they are now
Children's school and medical records where custody or maintenance is involved
Dates and names of the police stations or DLSA approached

escalation.where: Women helpline 181 / 1091, and the Protection Officer at the District Court
escalation.note: The Protection Officer assists in filing the DV Act application, free.

escalation.where: Police complaint (BNS / BNSS provisions) where there is cruelty or threat
escalation.note: Use the Police / FIR ladder if the station refuses.

escalation.where: Magistrate under the DV Act for protection, residence, custody and monetary orders
escalation.note: No court fee for a DV Act application.

escalation.where: Family Court / the personal-law forum for maintenance, divorce or custody
escalation.note: Personal law governs - a lawyer is essential here.

escalation.where: DLSA free legal aid (women are entitled without the income test)

deadlines.label: Most civil suits
deadlines.from: when the cause of action arose
deadlines.note: Contracts, money, damages and most possession claims run on three years; specific suits differ.

checklist: A one-page chronology with exact dates - the single most useful document in any case
Every agreement, invoice, notice and receipt, in date order
Copies of everything you sent, with the postal or delivery proof
Names, designations and addresses of the people involved
Identity and address proof of the complainant
Your own goal in one sentence: refund, apology, restoration, safety, or information

escalation.where: Written demand to the other party, with a deadline
escalation.note: Nearly every statute expects this first.

escalation.where: The regulator or ombudsman for that sector
escalation.note: Bank - RB-IOS; telecom - the operator + TRAI portal; electricity - the State Ombudsman.

escalation.where: RTI to get the official file notings behind a State action
escalation.note: Often the cheapest way to get the record.

escalation.where: Consumer forum / civil court / the special tribunal for the sector
DLSA free legal aid and the High Court's legal services clinic

letter_review_checklist: Is every date correct, and in the letter's own chronology order?
Is the addressee's designation and office exactly right (not a person's name)?
Is your name, address, phone and (where relevant) account/reference number filled in?
Does the letter state the specific relief you want, with a number where money is involved?
Is the legal citation actually applicable to your state / sector, and does it match the facts?
Are all attachments listed and enclosed, and does the letter refer to them as Annexures?
Is there a deadline for reply, and is it reasonable (7 to 15 days)?
Have you removed anger, abuse or threats - they hurt the eventual reading in court?
Have you kept a signed copy and the postal receipt with the tracking number?
Have you checked whether a lawyer or DLSA should look at it before it goes?
